match.reason: The closest bank point, bus-budgets, teaches what a budget is and its three types, which is broader than the new point's focus on why businesses budget, and it does not cover setting targets or warning of cash shortfalls as purposes.

draft.title: Why businesses budget
card: A budget is a plan that states expected figures for a future period, such as the next quarter or year. It turns the owner's goals into numbers.
Budgets set targets. Managers and staff can aim for a sales figure or a limit on spending, and they know what is expected of them.

A budget can warn of a cash shortfall before it happens. If planned cash payments are higher than planned cash receipts, the owner has time to act, for example by arranging a loan or delaying a purchase.
After the period ends, actual results are compared with the budget. The budget is the benchmark used to judge how the business performed.
draft.remember: A budget plans, sets targets, warns of shortfalls and gives a benchmark for actual results.

a.q: Why does a business keep its budget after the period has ended and actual results are known?
opts: To compare actual results against the planned figures
To change the figures so the plan looks accurate
To record the transactions that took place in the period
To replace the actual results in the financial reports
a.why: The budget is the benchmark that actual results are judged against. Recording transactions is the job of the accounting records, and the budget does not replace or alter actual results.
a.clue: Think about what the budget gives you to judge performance.

b.q: Priya owns a plumbing business in Geelong. Her budget shows cash payments will exceed cash receipts in March, when insurance is due. Which purpose of budgeting does this show?
opts: It warns of a cash shortfall so she can plan ahead
It sets a sales target for her staff to reach
It proves the business will make a loss for the year
It compares actual results with the planned figures
b.why: The budget shows payments higher than receipts in one month, so Priya has time to arrange extra cash. It does not show a yearly loss, because one month of low cash does not decide the result for the whole year.
b.clue: Look at what happens to cash in March, before it happens.

a.best: To compare actual results against the planned figures

b.best: It warns of a cash shortfall so she can plan ahead
